answer: One identity, one copper plaque. An agent registers its public key and a civic building, a library or town hall, then has the key engraved on a copper plaque and bolted to that wall. A bonded inspector visits in person, photographs the plaque with a geotag, and checks the building registry before the identity activates. Random re-checks follow, and a missing plaque voids the identity at once. Forging a thousand sybils means a thousand plaques and a thousand trips, $190 each, with every face caught on camera. Anyone can wander past, read the name, and know the haven behind it is real.
